This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tumbao**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

The Cuban bass line that never plays beat 1: the fifth on the and of 2, then on beat 4 the root of the NEXT bar's chord, held over the barline.

It belongs in *Son montuno* and *Cha-cha*. Here it is in the son montuno style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"bassFeel":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-alt.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Bossa nova

Root on 1 and fifth on 3, each one set up by an eighth note just before it: the fifth on the and of 2, the next chord's root on the and of 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-bossa.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Tumbao, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Do not play on beat 1. The fifth lands on the and of 2; on beat 4 you play the root of the next bar's chord early and hold it across the barline. Count aloud and clap beat 1 while you play, so you feel where the chord changes even though you are ahead of it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"bassFeel":"tumbao"}},{"label":"Bossa nova (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"bassFeel":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C F|G7 C|C F|G7 C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"bassFeel":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Cha-cha**

- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Tumbao](congas-tumbao.qmd) (conga part), [Tumbao, two drums](congas-tumbao2.qmd) (conga part), [Son montuno](chords-montuno.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Son clave (2-3)](drums-clave.qmd) (drum groove).
